items.mainDefect: In Google CalendarService.updateEvent, the fallback find compares calendar externalIds against an always-falsy externalCalendarId, so selectedCalendar is always undefined and calendarId: undefined gets sent to the update call.

secondary.defect: deleteEvent has the same dead find fallback, so its calendarId can never come from the destination calendar.

items.mainDefect: In Google CalendarService.updateEvent, the fallback find compares calendar externalIds against a null or empty externalCalendarId, so it can never match and calendarId becomes undefined.

secondary.defect: deleteEvent has the same dead find fallback, so deletes for references without externalCalendarId get an undefined calendarId.

items.mainDefect: In Google CalendarService.updateEvent, the fallback find predicate can never match because externalCalendarId is falsy in that branch, so updates go out with calendarId undefined.

secondary.defect: deleteEvent has the same dead predicate, so deletes are silently sent to the 'primary' calendar instead.

items.mainDefect: Office365 CalendarService always uses the first destination calendar's externalId, whichever team member's credential is running, so collective-event members get a 404 or a write to the wrong calendar.

secondary.defect: The larkcalendar service and the CalDAV base service also use the first destination calendar's externalId without matching it to the credential.
